item.title: Winning the Space Race Will Require a Diplomatic Victory at WRC-27
item.description: As China lands a reusable rocket and plans massive low-Earth orbit satellite constellations, the United States cannot take its lead in this critical technology for granted. Securing U.S. satellite leadership requires effective diplomacy before and during the 2027 World Radiocommunication Conference in Shanghai.

item.title: Rising U.S. Yields and Their Implications for Emerging Markets
item.description: Driven by real, inflation, and reaction-function shocks, the persistent rise in government bond yields since the February onset of conflict in the Middle East has mixed implications for emerging markets and developing economies.

item.title: Experts React: Takeaways from President Trump’s Trip to Asia
item.description: CSIS experts react to President Trump’s trip to China and share their reactions to the ASEAN Summit, Quad leaders’ meeting, APEC Summit, and Trump-Putin-Xi trilateral meeting.

item.title: After a Collapsed Bank and an Impeached President, What Lies Ahead for Paraguay?
item.description: The CSIS Americas Program explores the significance of Paraguay’s banking crisis and its regional implications.

item.title: Extreme Heat Is Already Dangerous to Americans. The Super El Niño Could Make Next Year Worse.
item.description: Heat from the Super El Niño, when combined with climate change, could set a new heat record in summer 2027. The arrival of new congressional members may provide an opportunity for Congress to protect Americans from the health impacts of extreme heat.

item.title: Mbappé’s Apology is a Warning: China’s Economic Coercion Needs a Collective Response
item.description: In Fortune, Victor Cha and Andy Lim argue that Mbappé’s apology is a warning to individuals, firms, and governments and China’s economic coercion needs a collective response.

item.title: The Cook Islands and the Future of Seabed Mining in the Pacific
item.description: The race for critical minerals is heating up in the Pacific, with the Cook Islands at the forefront of the debate between economic opportunity, environmental protection, and growing U.S.-China competition.
